evidence.finding: A user-configured notifications.json lists transports; a webhook transport POSTs the task notification event as JSON (with optional headers) and an exec transport runs a command with the event on stdin. Absent config the path is inert.

evidence.title: Remote access: notifications that reach you when nothing is open
evidence.locator: Notifications that reach you when nothing is open; A command or webhook
evidence.finding: Documents ~/.dev3.0/notifications.json with transports of kind webhook (POSTs the event JSON to a URL with optional headers) and exec, plus Web Push to a phone browser.

evidence.title: dev3.0 v1.65.2 README Telemetry
evidence.locator: README.md 'Telemetry' lines 371-394
evidence.finding: The app reports usage analytics; controls are the Settings → System → Telemetry toggle in any released build, DEV3_TELEMETRY=off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and the VITE_TELEMETRY=off build flag.

before.answer: Code, prompts, logs and artifacts stay on the machine except what the chosen agent CLIs send to their providers. Release builds send anonymous analytics to Google Analytics 4 and PostHog (no names, paths, prompts or diffs) with one switch, DEV3_TELEMETRY=off or DO_NOT_TRACK=1; a build from source has no PostHog key.

after.answer: Code, prompts, logs and artifacts stay on the machine except what the chosen agent CLIs send to their providers. Release builds send anonymous analytics to Google Analytics 4 and PostHog (no names, paths, prompts or diffs) with one switch, DEV3_TELEMETRY=off or DO_NOT_TRACK=1; a build from source has no PostHog key. Telemetry (atomic revision 2): on by default; the Settings, System, Telemetry toggle turns it off.
